answer: A proof-of-space protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to prove continuous custody of pre-plotted storage sectors. An attacker deploying cloned identities incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated non-volatile drive capacity per instance. Cryptographic integrity accretes slowly like a pearl, withstanding an adversarial traffic gale. A key limitation is that initializing storage plots moves like a glacier, excluding lightweight or transient agents.
